name: tr_podz
caption:
IF PODZ HAD A POKÉMON TEAM, HERE'S WHO WE'D SEND OUT 🎮🏀

🐣 Ducklett: better at swimming than flying. 1.4 points a game as a college freshman
🦢 Swanna: the one dancing in the middle leads the flock. WCC co-Player of the Year at Santa Clara
🐾 Eevee: unstable genes, so it can evolve in many ways. Pick #19, All-Rookie First Team
🛡️ Registeel: a body harder than any metal. All 82 games last season
🔥 Blaziken: the stronger the foe, the hotter it burns. Career-high 30 against Sacramento
🦊 Zoroark: its Illusion ability fools everyone. 16.8 points, 5.0 rebounds, 4.2 assists in his first 9 games

That's a party we'd take into any building. Which one would you swap in? 👇

Monster sprites: PMD Sprite Collab (sprites.pmdcollab.org), CC BY-NC 4.0

beats.vo: If Brandin Podziemski had a Pokemon team, here's what we'd be running.
beats.dlg: IF PODZ HAD A TEAM|OF MONSTERS...

beats.vo: First up, Ducklett. It's better at swimming than flying. One point four points a game as a college freshman.
Swanna. At dusk, the one dancing in the middle leads the whole flock. He transfers to Santa Clara and shares conference Player of the Year.
beats.dlg: IT LEADS THE FLOCK.|WCC CO-PLAYER OF THE YEAR!

beats.vo: Eevee. Its genes are unstable, so it can evolve in all kinds of ways. We took him nineteenth, and he made All-Rookie First Team.
beats.dlg: CAN EVOLVE IN MANY WAYS.|PICK 19: ALL-ROOKIE 1ST!

beats.vo: Registeel. Its body is harder than any kind of metal. All eighty-two games last season.
beats.dlg: HARDER THAN ANY METAL.|ALL 82 GAMES LAST SEASON!

beats.vo: Blaziken. The stronger the foe, the hotter its wrists burn. A career-high thirty points against Sacramento.
beats.dlg: BURNS HOTTER VS TOUGH FOES|CAREER-HIGH 30 VS SAC!

beats.vo: And the ace. Zoroark. Its ability, Illusion, fools everyone watching. Sixteen point eight points, five boards, four point two assists in his first nine games.
beats.dlg: ILLUSIONS FOOL EVERYONE.|16.8 PTS 5.0 REB 4.2 AST

facts.claim: Podziemski: 16 games off the bench as an Illinois freshman, 1.4 points per game; transferred to Santa Clara, WCC co-Player of the Year (2023); drafted 19th overall in 2023 by Golden State; NBA All-Rookie First (1st) Team (2024); April 10, 2026: career-high 30 points vs Sacramento; appeared in all 82 games in 2025-26
